title: Export Declaration Form (EDF): 2026 Filing Guide for India
summary: Learn what an Export Declaration Form (EDF) is, who needs to file it, 2026 deadlines, filing steps, documents, EDPMS, payment realisation, and closure.
body_markdown:
## **EDF Filing Deadline: When Do You Need to File It?**


For service and software exports, the **standard EDF filing deadline is within 30 days from the end of the month in which the invoice is raised.**


Exporters may submit one consolidated EDF for services exported to one or more overseas clients in a month, instead of filing separate EDFs. This is optional, not compulsory.


**EDF Filing Deadline Example:**


An Indian agency exports services and raises two invoices on 5 October and 23 October 2026.


-


**Invoice month ends:** 31 October 2026


-


**EDF filing deadline:** 30 November 2026


-


**Filing option:** One consolidated EDF covering both invoices


For services other than software, Regulation 3(2)(b) also permits EDF submission on or before receipt of payment. However, its interaction with the standard 30-day deadline may require clarification from your AD bank.


**As a precaution, aim to file within 30 days from the end of the invoice month unless your AD bank confirms a different permitted timeline.**


For goods exports, the EDF must be submitted at the time of export. At EDI ports, it is deemed submitted with the shipping bill, so no separate filing is required.


### **What Happens If You Don't File an EDF on Time?**


Missing an applicable EDF deadline may lead to bank follow-ups and compliance queries. For service exports, **Regulation 3(2)(c)** allows your Authorised Dealer (AD) bank to extend the filing deadline if it finds your reasons for the delay reasonable. Contact your bank promptly if you miss the deadline.


**Under Regulation 19(3)** , AD banks cannot impose charges or penalties for an exporter's regulatory delay or violation. However, statutory penalties may apply under Section 13 of[FEMA](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/understanding-fema-regulations-what-indian-exporters-need-to-know-about-its-impact-on-cross-border-payments) , 1999, following adjudication. There is no automatic fixed penalty for every late EDF filing.


## **Where and How to File an EDF**


The authority responsible for receiving your EDF depends on the type of export and where it takes place.


**Export Type**


**Where to File**


Goods exported through EDI ports


EDF is deemed submitted with the shipping bill. No separate filing is required.


Goods exported through non-EDI ports


Submit through Customs. The authenticated EDF is forwarded to the relevant AD bank.


Service exports from DTA


Submit to the Authorised Dealer (AD) bank.


Software exports from DTA


Submit through the AD bank or STPI, as applicable.


Exports from SEZs


Submit to the SEZ Development Commissioner, as applicable.


### **Which EDF Submission Process Does Your Bank Follow?**


The RBI prescribes the official EDF format, but Authorised Dealer (AD) banks may have different submission procedures and supporting document requirements.


Before filing, check with your AD bank:


-


**Submission method:** Whether the EDF is accepted through email, an online portal or a bank branch.


-


**Required documents:** Whether invoices, contracts or additional bank-specific declarations are needed.


-


**Processing details:** How submission is acknowledged, expected processing timelines and any applicable charges.


Under Regulation 19 of the 2026 RBI regulations, AD banks must publish their policy and the main features of their standard operating procedure (SOP) on their websites.


If you receive international payments through a payment platform, confirm where your EDF should be submitted and which AD bank handles EDPMS reporting and payment reconciliation.


## **How to Fill an Export Declaration Form: Step-by-Step**


The official 2026 EDF contains separate sections for goods and service exports. Complete the sections applicable to your transaction, ensuring the details match your invoices and supporting records.


**Watch the video below for a visual walkthrough, then follow the steps to complete your EDF.**


**Before You Start: Details to Keep Ready**


-


Exporter name, address, PAN, IEC and GSTIN, as applicable


-


Overseas customer and invoice details


-


Invoice currency, amount and goods or service description


-


Applicable HSN or SAC classification


-


AD bank name and AD code


-


Contracts, shipping records or other supporting documents, where applicable


Your AD bank may request additional documents depending on the transaction.


### **Step 1: Complete Section 1 - General Information**


Enter your export type, exporter name and address, PAN, IEC and GSTIN, as applicable.


Provide your AD bank name and[AD code](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/ad-code) , mode of transport or delivery, mode of realisation, consignee details and any applicable third-party payer information.


The form also asks for the total FOB/services value in INR, written in words. For foreign-currency invoices, confirm the appropriate conversion basis with your AD bank.


### **Step 2: Complete Section 2A - Goods Export Details**


For goods exports requiring a separate EDF, enter the overseas buyer's details, invoice number, date, currency, amount and relevant[HSN classification](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/hsn-code-meaning-finder-guide-for-indian-businesses) .


Include the applicable contract and payment terms, goods export value, freight, insurance, commission and other adjustments. Section 2A is repeated for each invoice under a shipping bill.


For applicable postal or courier exports, enter the foreign post office or courier name and parcel receipt number and date in Section 3. The Authorised Dealer completes the stamp and signature in this section.


For goods exported through EDI ports, the EDF is deemed submitted with the shipping bill, so a separate EDF is not required.


### **Step 3: Complete Section 2B - Service Export Details**


For service and software exports, Section 2B records the details and declared value of the services supplied. Enter the relevant information for each invoice.


**Field**


**What to Enter**


Service recipient


Overseas customer's name, address and country


Invoice details


Invoice number and date


Currency and amount


Invoice currency and value


Net realisable value


Value expected to be realised after applicable adjustments, if any


Contract details


Contract number and date, if any


Service description


Nature of the services provided


SAC code


Applicable Service Accounting Code


Remarks


Additional information, where relevant


**SAC code vs RBI purpose code:** A SAC code classifies the exported service and is a field in Section 2B. An RBI purpose code identifies the nature of an international remittance and is not a separate field in Section 2B.


### **Step 4: Review and Sign the Declaration**


Verify the exporter and recipient details, invoice references, classifications and declared values.


Complete **Section 4 - Declaration by the Exporters** , including the applicable undertaking, export realisation deadline, date and signature. Confirm the correct realisation deadline with your AD bank.


Leave Section 5, which is reserved for the specified authority, for that authority to complete.


### **Step 5: Submit the EDF**


Submit the completed EDF to the applicable authority within the prescribed filing deadline. Keep a copy of the declaration, supporting[invoices](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/commercial-invoice-for-export) , and submission acknowledgement. The relevant AD bank handles EDPMS reporting and payment reconciliation.


### **EDF Form Sample: One EDF for Multiple Service Invoices**


Suppose ABC Digital Pvt Ltd provides marketing services to two overseas clients in October 2026.


**Invoice**


**Date**


**Overseas client**


**Amount**


INV-101


8 October 2026


US Client A


USD 2,500


INV-102


20 October 2026


UK Client B


GBP 1,200


Assuming both are covered service exports, the company may submit one consolidated EDF for October, entering each invoice separately in Section 2B.


Each invoice retains its original currency and value. For the total services value in INR required in Section 1, the company must convert the invoice values using a basis accepted by its AD bank.

**Common Mistake**


**Possible Issue**


**How to Avoid It**


Calculating 30 days from the invoice date


Incorrect service-export filing deadline


Calculate the standard deadline from the end of the invoice month


Incorrect SAC or HSN code


Classification queries or corrections


Verify the applicable classification before filing


Invoice value or currency mismatch

Ensure EDF details match the original invoice

Confirm the relevant AD bank and AD code


Using an outdated EDF form

Use the official 2026 EDF Annex


Assuming payment automatically closes EDPMS

Confirm that your AD bank has reconciled the payment and updated or closed the EDPMS entry


## **What Happens After You File the EDF?**


After submitting an EDF, your export details are recorded in the **Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS)** . Your Authorised Dealer (AD) bank handles the applicable reporting and payment reconciliation.


For service exports, the AD bank must enter EDF details into[EDPMS](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/idpms-vs-edpms-essential-rbi-guide-for-exporters) within five working days of receiving the declaration from the exporter.


When payment arrives, the bank verifies the remittance and updates or closes the EDPMS entry once the applicable requirements are met.


Payment received does not always mean EDPMS closed. Keep your EDF, invoices and remittance records. If an entry remains outstanding, contact your AD bank.


### **How Does the ₹10 Lakh EDPMS Closure Rule Work?**


Under Regulation 4(2), first proviso, AD banks may close eligible EDPMS entries for goods shipping bills or service invoices valued at ₹10 lakh or less (or the foreign-currency equivalent), based on the exporter's declaration about payment realisation.


These declarations may also be submitted quarterly for bulk closure. For example, an exporter raises three invoices worth ₹4 lakh, ₹8 lakh and ₹9 lakh. Each meets the ₹10 lakh value threshold, even though their combined value is ₹21 lakh. A separate ₹12 lakh invoice does not qualify for this simplified closure provision.


Under Regulation 6, proviso, declaration-based reductions in export value may also be permitted for eligible shipping bills or invoices within the same threshold.


On 7 October 2026, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra was reported as saying that small exporters can give a self-declaration for bills up to ₹10 lakh. Confirm with your AD bank which supporting documents it requires.


**These provisions simplify EDPMS closure and reduce certain export realisation requirements.** They do not exempt exporters from applicable EDF filing requirements or the 9-month and 12-month payment realisation deadlines.


## **What Happens If Your Export Payment Is Delayed or Not Fully Received?**


Exporters must realise and repatriate their export proceeds within the applicable deadline, even after filing an EDF. **If payment is delayed, partially received, or not received, the export entry may remain outstanding until the payment or shortfall is resolved.**


**Example:** If your invoice is USD 10,000 and you receive USD 7,000, you may still need to reconcile or regularise the remaining USD 3,000.


Contact your AD bank, preferably before the deadline, with the invoice, payment records and reasons for the shortfall. The bank may approve an extension under Regulation 5 or a reduction in export value under Regulation 6, subject to its assessment.


Under Regulation 13, if export proceeds remain unrealised for more than one year beyond the applicable deadline or approved extension, further exports are permitted only against full advance payment or an irrevocable Letter of Credit.


### **What is the Export Payment Realisation Period in 2026?**


Under Regulation 5, export proceeds must generally be realised and repatriated within:


-


**9 months:** From the shipment date for goods or the invoice date for services.


-


**12 months:** For qualifying exports invoiced or settled in Indian rupees (INR).


For goods exported to overseas warehouses, the period starts from the **date of sale of the goods from the warehouse.** For project exports, the contract's payment terms apply.


The original 2026 Regulations provided 15 and 18 months. The amendment dated 22 September 2026 reduced these to 9 and 12 months before the Regulations came into force on 1 October 2026.

## **Frequently Asked Questions About EDF Filing**


### **1. What is the full form of EDF?**


EDF stands for **Export Declaration Form** , a declaration used to report the value and details of goods, services, and software exported from India under FEMA.


### **2. Do freelancers need to file an EDF?**


On 7 October 2026, RBI officials stated that individuals undertaking transactions of a personal nature need not report them under the new framework. This was a public clarification, not an express exemption in the Regulations. Freelancers undertaking commercial exports should confirm the applicable requirements with their AD bank.


### **3. Is SOFTEX still required after 1 October 2026?**


For software exports covered by the new 2026 Regulations, EDF replaces the earlier[SOFTEX declaration](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/softex-for-indian-exporters) requirement. Software exporters should follow the applicable EDF submission process through their AD bank, STPI or SEZ authority.


### **4. Can I fill and submit an EDF form online?**


You can prepare an EDF online using Infinity's free EDF Generator for service and software exporters. However, preparation and submission are separate steps. Confirm the accepted submission method with your AD bank or specified authority.


### **5. How can I find my AD bank for EDF filing?**


Your relevant AD bank handles the foreign exchange transaction and associated reporting. Don't rely solely on the bank named on your FIRA, especially when using a payment platform. Confirm with your receiving bank or payment provider; Infinity's team can also help.


### **6. Can an EDF be amended after submission?**


If you discover an error, contact your AD bank or the relevant specified authority. They can guide you through the applicable correction process and supporting documents.


### **7. Is EDF filing required if my international payment is settled in INR?**


Yes, if the export is otherwise subject to EDF reporting. INR settlement does not automatically exempt it. Qualifying exports invoiced or settled in INR have a 12-month payment realisation period.


### **8. What is the difference between EDF, EDPMS, FIRA and eBRC?**


-


**EDF:** Declares export details and value under FEMA.


-


**EDPMS:** Records and monitors export transactions and outstanding entries.


-


**FIRA:** Documents an inward foreign remittance.


-


**eBRC:** Evidences export payment realisation for applicable purposes through the DGFT system.


### **9. Does EDF filing replace GST or income tax reporting?**


No. EDF filing is a FEMA export-reporting requirement.[GST](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/gst-e-invoicing) and income tax obligations are separate, although relevant invoice and transaction records should remain consistent.
